rawCommits.subject: fix(sessions): keep new chat highlighted across optimistic→real swap
rawCommits.body:
After SessionReady, `useNewSessionUrlSync` did two things in sequence:

  1. `optimisticRow.swap(<real-id>)` — synchronously rewrote the
     `optimistic:<uuid>` row in `sessionsBySurface` to the
     server-assigned UUID via Zustand `setState`.
  2. `setSearchParams({ session: <real-id> })` — queued a React
     Router navigate.

`SessionsList`'s `effectiveSelectedSessionId` only had two cases — URL
session, or fall back to the optimistic row. The window between those
two writes (and any subsequent render where the router state hadn't
propagated through `useSearchParams` yet — back/forward, suspended tab,
etc.) had neither: the row was no longer `optimistic:` and `?session=`
hadn't landed, so the just-created session visibly appeared at the top
of the list with its server-generated title but read as unselected.
The user reported this as "after sending message in new session, still
does not select it in the css".

Add a third fallback: when the URL has no `?session=` and no optimistic
row exists, highlight `titledRows[0]` — the newest row in the surface.
The surfaces are stored in `sortSessionsDesc` order from
`loadAgentSessions` / `loadProjectSessions`, and `addOptimisticSession`
stamps `started_at` at insert time, so the just-swapped real-id row
always sorts to the top across the swap window. Pre-swap, the
optimistic branch still wins; once the URL settles, the explicit
`selectedSessionId` branch wins again.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep new chat highlighted across optimistic→real swap

rawCommits.subject: feat(swarm): auto-recover once on initial-provision failure and surface swarm error
rawCommits.body:
When a brand-new remote agent's background readiness wait timed out or
saw `state: error`, the only effect was a `warn!` in the desktop log:
the agent stayed in `provisioning`, the UI sat indefinitely on
"Starting up...", and the user had to manually click Recovery (often
not even knowing the agent was stuck). The cause string supplied by
aura-swarm (e.g. an `Unschedulable` PodScheduled message) was also
dropped because `SwarmAgentStateResponse` only deserialized `state`,
so any error event the gateway emitted was reduced to a generic
"entered error state".

Changes:

- Widen `SwarmAgentStateResponse` to include `error_message` and
  carry the optional reason through `SwarmAgentReadyError::ErrorState`
  and `PollOutcome::Errored`.
- Replace the inert `warn!()` branches in `spawn_swarm_readiness_check`
  with `auto_recover_after_initial_failure`, which broadcasts an
  `auto_recover/starting` event, runs the existing
  `recover_remote_agent_pipeline` exactly once, and on failure
  broadcasts a terminal `state: "error", phase: "startup_failed"`
  carrying both the original swarm reason and the recovery error so
  the StatusCard exits the indeterminate provisioning state and shows
  the manual Recovery action.
- Update `handle_recovery_readiness_error` to embed the swarm-supplied
  reason in both the broadcast banner and the `ApiError`, so the
  manual Recovery click also surfaces the descriptive cause.
- Pass enough context (cloned `AppState`, `Arc<NetworkClient>`,
  `NetworkAgent`) through `BackgroundReadinessTask` to invoke recovery
  from the spawned task.
- Add `starting` and `startup_failed` entries to the StatusCard
  `PHASE_NOTICES` so the UI labels match the new broadcast phases.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: auto-recover once on initial-provision failure and surface swarm error

rawCommits.subject: feat(agent-picker): add searchable AgentSelectorList with keyboard nav
rawCommits.body:
New `AgentSelectorList` component renders the Telegram-style picker
the next step will mount inside `AgentSelectorModal`. The list shows a
'Standard Agent' row at the top followed by every saved fleet agent,
filtered live by the search query (case-insensitive over name + role).

Keyboard model mirrors `SlashCommandMenu`:
- Up/Down move the active highlight, wrapping at the edges
- Enter activates the highlighted row
- Escape calls the supplied `onCancel`
- Mouse hover updates the active index
- Rows fire on `mouseDown` with `preventDefault` so the search input
  keeps focus when a row is clicked

The component is purely presentational; it forwards a ref so the
parent modal can hand it the focus target via `Modal.initialFocusRef`.
Per-row `creating` state shows a spinner on the row mid-create and
disables every row to prevent double-fires.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(installer): un.-prefix MUI_CUSTOMFUNCTION_UNGUIINIT callback
rawCommits.body:
makensis aborted while expanding MUI_LANGUAGE -> MUI_UNFUNCTION_GUIINIT
because the uninstaller's GUI-init callback (AuraUnOnGUIInit) was
emitted as a Call inside the uninstaller section, which NSIS rejects
unless the target function name starts with "un.". Renamed
AuraUnOnGUIInit -> un.AuraOnGUIInit at both the !define and the Function
declaration, and documented the constraint inline so it doesn't regress.

rawCommits.subject: fix(projects): default sidekick tab to Terminal on app entry
rawCommits.body:
The shared sidekick store persists its active tab to localStorage and is
also mutated by the Tasks app (writes "tasks") and the spec-generation
stream (writes "specs"). Once a user clicked Sessions in Projects, that
value stuck across reloads and other apps could pollute it, so Projects
no longer reliably landed on Terminal.

Force ProjectMainPanel to call setActiveTab("terminal") once per mount,
guarded by a ref so switching tabs inside the session still persists.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(agents): stabilize project agent picker size and show full org fleet
rawCommits.body:
The project sidebar's Add Agent picker (AgentSelectorModal) was resizing
between loading and loaded states, again after a row was selected (the
just-clicked agent disappeared once it landed in agentsByProject), and
in some cases flashed "No agents match your search." for a frame when
that row was the only match. It also only fetched agents the current
user authored, hiding teammates' shared agents that the Agents app
sidebar surfaces.

- Pass activeOrg.org_id to api.agents.list() in useAgentSelectorData so
  the picker shows the full org fleet (matching useAgentStore.fetchAgents).
- Wrap the loading/empty/list region in a new .pickerBody with a 360px
  min-height floor (waived inside the mobile drawer) so the modal keeps
  the same vertical footprint across states.
- Track recentlySelectedId in AgentSelectorModal and exclude it from
  the assigned-agents filter, keeping the row visible during the
  create+handoff transition and preventing the empty-state flash.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: stabilize project agent picker size and show full org fleet

rawCommits.subject: chore(changelog-media): tag credit-low errors with the failing provider
rawCommits.body:
The publish-release-changelog-media workflow calls three different paid
APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Browser Use). When one runs out of credits, the
previous wording made it ambiguous which account actually needed a top-up
- e.g. "You need at least $1.00 in credits. Current balance: $0.34" with
no provider name attached.

Route every HTTP/SDK failure in the pipeline through a shared helper that
prefixes the failing provider and names the env var to top up:

  [Browser Use] credit balance is too low (top up the account tied to
  BROWSER_USE_API_KEY - https://cloud.browser-use.com/billing): You need
  at least $1.00 in credits. Current balance: $0.34

Non-credit failures also pick up the provider tag so CI logs always
identify the source.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: tag credit-low errors with the failing provider

rendered.title: Searchable agent picker, sturdier Windows installer, and clearer recovery paths
rendered.intro: Today's nightly centers on a redesigned Add Agent picker for projects — a Telegram-style searchable list with a one-key Standard Agent shortcut — alongside meaningful reliability work: the Windows installer's themed bitmaps and uninstaller callback are fixed, stuck remote agents now auto-recover and surface real swarm errors, and a regression that handed every new agent full capabilities is rolled back.

entries.title: Redesigned Add Agent picker with search and keyboard nav
entries.summary: The project Add Agent flow becomes a searchable Telegram-style list with a one-press Standard Agent shortcut, plus fixes for installer theming and stuck remote agents.

items.text: The Add Agent modal swaps its grid of cards for an autofocused search input and a vertical list — a top 'Standard Agent' row plus the user's fleet — navigable with arrow keys and Enter, with case-insensitive filtering over name and role. The old '+ Create New Agent' footer and editor detour are gone; pressing Enter on the Standard row spawns a generic agent through the same endpoint the project-row '+' used to call directly.

Fixed a long-standing glitch where a newly created session briefly appeared unselected after sending its first message: SessionsList now falls back to the newest row in the surface during the optimistic-to-real id swap window, so the freshly created chat stays highlighted across the transition.

Windows installer now stages dark and light themed bitmaps directly into $PLUGINSDIR instead of root-relative paths, hardens light-bitmap derivation with explicit preprocessor errors, swaps the header bitmap at GUI init for light mode, and extends the dark title-bar hook to the uninstaller.

Remote agents that fail their initial provision no longer sit forever on 'Starting up…': the server now auto-recovers once on initial-provision failure, and if that also fails it broadcasts a terminal startup_failed state carrying the swarm's actual reason (e.g. an Unschedulable PodScheduled message) instead of a generic error, so the StatusCard exits limbo and shows manual Recovery with the real cause.

entries.title: Chat, sidebar, and permissions polish
entries.summary: A cluster of fixes around chat errors, the projects sidebar, session rows, and a rolled-back permissions default.

items.text: Chat now surfaces a helpful error when a message is sent to an agent that isn't assigned to a project, instead of failing silently.
The Add Agent modal can no longer get wedged: Close and Escape are no longer blocked by stale busy state, and the Create button is only disabled during an actual in-flight API call.
Navigating into a project now auto-expands its tree in the sidebar to reveal the active agent, and session rows show their project name when the visible sessions span more than one project.

Reverted a regression that quietly handed every new agent full capabilities: non-CEO agents once again start with an empty permission bundle and must opt in through the Permissions tab, while the CEO bootstrap and project-scoped self-caps splice are preserved.

entries.title: Uninstaller GUI-init callback no longer aborts makensis
entries.summary: A second installer fix unblocks Windows builds by satisfying NSIS's naming rule for uninstaller callbacks.

items.text: makensis was aborting while expanding MUI_LANGUAGE because the uninstaller's GUI-init callback was emitted as a Call inside the uninstaller section without the required 'un.' prefix. Renaming AuraUnOnGUIInit to un.AuraOnGUIInit at both the !define and the Function declaration restores the Windows installer build.

entries.title: Project agent picker stability and copy cleanup
entries.summary: Follow-up polish on the new Add Agent picker plus small but visible project-sidebar tweaks.

items.text: The project Add Agent picker now shows the full org fleet (matching the Agents app sidebar) instead of only agents the current user authored, keeps a stable 360px-tall body across loading, empty, and loaded states, and no longer flashes 'No agents match your search' or hides the just-selected row during the create+handoff transition.

The Projects sidebar reliably opens on the Terminal tab again: ProjectMainPanel now pins the shared sidekick store to 'terminal' once per mount, so writes from the Tasks app or spec-generation stream no longer leak across reloads.
The agent context-menu action in the Projects sidebar is now labeled 'Remove from Project', matching the existing modal copy and clarifying that the removal is project-scoped.

entries.title: Changelog-media CI names the provider when credits run out
entries.summary: Release tooling now identifies which paid API account needs a top-up when the changelog-media workflow fails.

items.text: Every HTTP/SDK failure in the publish-release-changelog-media pipeline now flows through a shared helper that prefixes the failing provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, or Browser Use) and names the env var to top up, so a low-credit error in CI logs reads like '[Browser Use] credit balance is too low (top up the account tied to BROWSER_USE_API_KEY …)' instead of an unattributed balance message. Non-credit failures also pick up the provider tag.

highlights: New searchable, keyboard-driven Add Agent picker
Windows installer no longer aborts on uninstaller GUI init
Stuck remote agents auto-recover with a real error message
Non-CEO agents go back to empty-by-default permissions
